name: Swift-Qwen3.8-27b
context_scaling: Inherited unchanged from Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B (config.json max_position_embeddings 262144). This derivative does not publish a context-extension recipe of its own.
attention_variant: hybrid: Gated DeltaNet linear attention with full gated attention every 4th layer (16 of 64); partial RoPE
notes: ADDED 2026-11-15. A finetune of Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B, not a new base model: same config.json, same 27.781 parameters (identical tensor set). Recorded as a contender because it publishes benchmark evidence against its own base; the evidence rows below are card-sourced and marked vendor_claim. Licence other, repo created 2026-09-08.

benchmarks.name: C-Eval
benchmarks.config: Card HTML table 'Benchmark / Score', columns 'Base' vs 'Swift'. Base 90.00 -> Swift 90.62 (+0.62pp). Real base run: the card's own column, same harness and same output cap (16,384) for both columns; greedy not stated.

benchmarks.name: LiveCodeBench v6
benchmarks.config: Same table, LiveCodeBench v6 row. Base 76.76 -> Swift 81.55 (+4.79pp), the largest win. Output cap 32,768 printed for both columns. This is the only row where Swift is materially better rather than level.

benchmarks.name: GPQA-Diamond
benchmarks.config: LOSES to its own base: base 88.38 vs Swift 88.28 (-0.10pp), within noise. Output cap 100,000 for both.

benchmarks.name: MMLU-Pro
benchmarks.config: LOSES: base 85.47 vs Swift 84.95 (-0.52pp). Same table, output cap 100,000.

benchmarks.name: IFBench
benchmarks.config: LOSES: base 73.53 vs Swift 71.80 (-1.73pp). Output cap 81,920. Instruction following is the clearest regression in the table.

benchmarks.name: AIME 2026
benchmarks.config: LOSES: base 98.67 vs Swift 94.00 (-4.67pp) - the widest loss. Output cap 250,000. Token cut on this row is -26.7% mean / -50.2% median thinking tokens, so the accuracy drop buys the token saving.

benchmarks.name: HMMT Nov 2025
benchmarks.config: LOSES: base 99.33 vs Swift 96.00 (-3.33pp). Output cap 250,000.

benchmarks.name: ERQA
benchmarks.config: LOSES: base 67.45 vs Swift 66.30 (-1.15pp), multimodal row. Output cap 100,000.

benchmarks.name: Terminal-Bench 2.1
benchmarks.config: LOSES: base 66.74 vs Swift 65.84 (-0.90pp). Agent/task limits rather than a token cap. Agentic coding is the use case the token saving is aimed at, and it still drops slightly.
